name: u00
explanation: Token-level detector for the head word of a courtesy formula of gratitude, apology or hope: it fires on the word token itself (Thanks/thanks/Thank/thank, Apologies/apology/apologize, Sorry, grateful, hope/hopes/hoping/Hopefully), about 0.6-0.8 of max and strongest on a line-initial 'Thanks' sign-off, and is near zero on the following tokens and on other polite words (appreciate, Cheers, Pardon, Welcome, regret) and on compounds/derivations such as 'Thanksgiving' or 'hopeless'. A smaller unrelated offshoot set of single tokens (' payment', ' boot', ' recovery', ' due') also fires at a similar level regardless of context.

name: u01
explanation: A diffuse, context-wide dial rather than a token detector: once a text has run for roughly 20+ tokens it sits at 0.1-0.5 of max on many tokens and peaks near max on the second newline of a paragraph break (the '\n' token right before a new paragraph's first word), on subword pieces of rare words or names ('atic', 'ar' in Mush-ar-raf, 'ition'), and on citation pieces (' et' in 'X et al.', page numbers). Its overall level depends heavily on how the text opens: a fragment or mid-sentence start (' had a...', ' mRNA and...') or an opener such as 'Various', 'Several', 'In/On/As a ...' raises the whole text, while texts that open with a pronoun subject plus verb ('She closed', 'We talked', 'It had') or that are short simple sentences stay near zero.

name: u02
explanation: Fires on a '.' written with no space directly after a word or initial, inside a dotted identifier where more text follows at once: attribute access (sys.argv), file names and extensions (main.rb, __init__.py), initials (J.K.), version strings (3.0.4). It is strongest on the first such dot after a short word in code or a file path, and stays near zero on sentence-final periods. A weaker secondary trigger is ' opening' in box-office phrasing ('in its opening weekend/frame'), plus some command-line flag dashes (' -y', 'curl -X').

name: u03
explanation: Fires on the token of a form of the verb 'be' used as a copula or auxiliary (is, are, am, was, were, be, been, being, and contracted 're / 's), at roughly 0.35-0.65 of max for ordinary uses and highest (0.8-0.9+) on a contracted 're after a pronoun (you/they/we're, especially with a curly apostrophe) and on 'is'/'s after 'what' (what on earth is, what's). Other contracted auxiliaries ('ve, 'll, 's of it's) get weaker activity (~0.3-0.4), 'm is weak, and non-'be' verbs in the same slot (has, does, went, like, made, seems) are near zero.

name: u04
explanation: Fires on the last word of a discourse connective that opens a clause or follows a comma and announces an addition, enumeration, example or emphasis: 'of course', 'For instance', 'First(ly)/First off/Secondly', 'Moreover', 'In addition', 'as well (as)', 'especially/particularly', 'in particular', 'On top of that'. It often carries over onto the following comma. It stays near zero on the same words used literally (for example 'the course was hard', 'It first raises') and on contrastive or attitude connectives such as 'However' or 'Sadly'.

name: u05
explanation: Context-start detector: fires on the first one to three tokens of a text when the text opens mid-stream with a space-prefixed lowercase word (as when a window cuts into a sentence, e.g. ' in spirit', ' hybrid', ' poor', ' hopes', ' b'), peaking on the first content word and decaying within a few tokens; it is near silent once a few tokens of ordinary context have been read, and much weaker when the text opens like a normal document start (a capitalised or unspaced first token such as 'The', 'Hybrid'). Strength varies by word (e.g. ' poor' strong, ' rich' weak); a few mid-document peaks (' Giant'/' Windsor' in heading lists, ' U' in code, ' (' before an acronym) are leftovers it does not explain.

name: u06
explanation: A diffuse layer-1 formatting unit: it fires most on structured markup and code, peaking on the token after '#' in a curly-brace anchor id such as '{#sec1}' after a heading word (the digit or 'sec'), and on the individual ' ' tokens inside runs of space indentation in code, XML or JSON (not on tab indentation). It is near zero on the same content written as plain prose punctuation, e.g. '(sec 1)' or '[sec1]', and gives only weak, scattered activity (below about a third of max) on ordinary narrative prose tokens.

name: u07
explanation: Fires on a short word-start fragment (2-3 letters or a lone capital, e.g. ' K', 'tra', 'ery', 'Rel', 'TS', 'ut' in Bh|ut|to) of a familiar word or name that the tokenizer has split atypically because a bracket, slash, space token or ALL-CAPS took away the word's usual leading-space token, so the rest of the word is still to come (ANY K|IND, [tra|iler, ery|thema, Object/Rel|ational, (TS|X). It is weaker in fixed license boilerplate (distributed in the / under the, "AS IS") and is near zero on whole-word tokens and on long or rare fragments (fluor-our-ac-il, Aeg-im-ius, Von-neg-ut).

name: u08
explanation: A dense, weakly selective dial rather than a token detector. It is strongest in the first two positions of a text when the text opens with certain content fragments, above all ' wash' (as in ' wash'/'rooms', ' wash the car'). That opening state keeps all later tokens of a short text raised (about 0.3-0.6 of max). Away from the text start it stays low (<0.3) in short text and climbs slowly over roughly the first 50-100 tokens of long expository or technical documents. There it peaks on mid-clause tokens: the plural present copula ' are' (much more than ' is'/' were'), second subword pieces ('rooms', 'pper', 'ull', 'ist') and relative/purpose words (' which', ' to', ' producing').

name: u09
explanation: A diffuse, context-driven retrospective dial with no fixed trigger token: it is silent on short texts (roughly the first 20-30 tokens) and on most tokens, and fires sporadically on (a) a determiner ' the'/' a' right after a preposition or verb in running prose (connect to| the, On| the, focused onto| the, take| the) and (b) short abbreviations or first subword pieces of technical terms (NK, the digit of CD8, tex, Alt, v); these spikes grow with the amount of preceding same-topic technical context in the window and are weaker after off-topic context.

name: u10
explanation: Layer-0 token detector centred on the word ' and' as a coordinating conjunction. It fires most when ' and' closes a series ('longer, wider, and lower', '60, 90, and 120') inside a longer stretch of prose. It fires more weakly on list-separating commas and on a few idiosyncratic single tokens (' cis', Spanish ' es', sentence-initial ' Therefore', ' Noble'). Other connectives (' or', '&', ' yet', ' plus', ' but') get roughly a third to two thirds of the response, and the token after ' and' does not matter (retrospective). The strength is modulated by the earlier context (about 0.3-0.5 of max in short sentences, up to about 0.9 in long technical or descriptive prose), so predict active mainly on ' and' and series commas.

name: u11
explanation: Fires on the head noun of a definite time-reference phrase ('the time', 'the next day', 'The night', 'the moment', 'the 1919 New Year') or a definite framing noun ('the fact', 'The reason'), and on temporal subordinators 'since' (strongest after 'Ever'), 'before' and 'that' in 'now that'. The same nouns stay near zero after an indefinite or quantifying determiner ('a time', 'a moment', 'a day ago', 'last year', 'once upon a time'), as do 'after', 'until', 'when', 'because' and complementizer 'that' ('I know that').

name: u12
explanation: Fires in a business/commercial context on the slot where a company or organisation name is expected and on the tokens of that name, especially its later sub-word or second word (e.g. 'owned by' / 'sold to' / 'acquired by' / 'published by' then 'Jackson Family', 'Smith & Sons', 'KPM|G', 'Newsp|apers'), anticipating a corporate continuation such as Inc, Holdings, Industries, Wines. The same name or the same 'by'/'to' gives little or nothing when the frame is non-commercial (eaten by, read by, written by, with his sons, my friend).

name: u13
explanation: Largely a positional dial: the pole is strongest on whichever token sits about 36-41 tokens after the start of the context (smaller bumps near positions 72 and 102-103), and tokens elsewhere seldom pass about 0.3 of max. Inside that band, content-bearing continuation tokens (a name opening a new paragraph, a verb or preposition right after a subject or title noun, a word's second sub-token, a closing ')' or '?') reach 0.6-1.0 of max. Moving the same token a few positions out of the band, by adding or removing tokens earlier in the text, drops it sharply; same-length word swaps barely change it.

name: u14
explanation: Fires on the joining token that opens a value or argument in PHP/shell/HTML-style code: '($' after a method or function name, ' =' after a $variable, '="' after an HTML attribute, '-X' after curl. It also fires on the hyphen right after a negating or graded prefix in a compound modifier ('non-', 'high-', 'low-'). Activation is strongest in a code-like or legal-boilerplate context. It stays near zero on ordinary prose, on hyphens in fixed phrases ('state-of-the-art', 'top-quality', numeric ranges), and when the operator is replaced by a non-opening one ('+', '[', or a space).

name: u15
explanation: Fires on the articles ' the' / ' a' (weakly, about 0.3-0.6 of max, on almost any article) and fires strongly (above 0.75 of max) when the article comes straight after a verb or preposition that opens a fixed manner/comparison idiom, so that 'same', 'way', 'right/wrong way' or 'bit' is the expected next word: 'stayed/look/remained the [same]', 'go the [right way]', 'do it the [way]', 'in a [way]', 'quite a [bit]', 'part of a [larger]'. Non-article words in the same slot ('some', 'this', 'so', 'alike') stay near zero, and the following adjective ('same', 'right', 'larger') gets only a weaker echo.

name: u16
explanation: A dense, broadly active pole whose baseline rises with depth into the text (near zero on the first 2-3 tokens, about 0.3-0.5 of max a dozen or more tokens in). It peaks above that baseline on word-internal joins: the plural enzyme suffix 'ases' (kinases, lipases, phosphatases, but not singular 'ase'), and a hyphen joining a compound word or number range (state-of-the-art, navbar-fixed-top, 7-8). Spaced versions of the same words, and ordinary whole words, stay at the baseline.

name: u17
explanation: Fires on the token right after a vague, large or whole-amount quantifier, which is usually the partitive ' of' (or a possessive or determiner such as ' my' or ' the'), when it completes a quantity phrase like 'a number of', 'a lot of', 'a good deal of', 'most of', 'much of', 'all of', 'many of', 'a variety of', 'the rest of' or 'all my'. It also fires weaker on the quantifier noun itself ('number', 'lot'). It stays near zero on ' of' after ordinary nouns ('a list of', 'a jar of', 'the top of'), after 'one of' and in phrases with no quantifier.

name: u18
explanation: A broad, context-depth dial: near zero for the first ~15-20 tokens of a text that opens at a clean sentence start, then noisy low-to-moderate activity on most tokens as context grows. Its strongest peaks sit on a delimiting/selecting premodifier that opens a noun phrase after a determiner or preposition (last, past, only, least, first, final, whole, each, latest, long-term), rather than on the head noun or on ordinary descriptive adjectives (new, recent), which stay at the background level.

name: u19
explanation: Fires on the connector token that opens an optional attachment after a phrase that is already complete: in prose, an adjunct preposition (on/at/for/during/by/in introducing a date, time, condition, purpose or agent) after a finished verb+object or place-name phrase, plus verbs like 'signifies'/'tells' that take a following object; in code, the '_' that extends an identifier prefix (array_, layout_, table_) or the 'function' keyword after '='. It stays near zero on prepositions that are required complements of the verb (put/placed ... on, looked at, depends on) and on ordinary content words.

name: u20
explanation: Fires on the bare word-internal subword tokens 'il', 'ic' and 'oph' (also uppercase 'IL'/'IC') when they continue a word split into fragments, typically in a rare name, foreign word or technical term (Watt|w|il, Z|il|vold, roland|ic, Okada|ic, oes|oph|ageal, te|il|weise). It stays near zero on whole words that merely contain these letters (' ill', ' oil', ' iconic', ' logic', ' pencil', ' Brazilian'), on space-prefixed ' il'/' ic', and on other word-internal fragments such as 'al', 'el', 'ec', 'om'.

name: u21
explanation: Fires on the first token of the second conjunct of a tight two-part coordination, the word right after 'and', 'or' or a pairing comma, when the conjuncts are parallel modifiers, quantities or antonym/idiom pairs (more and [more], hour or [two], quickly and [easily], black and [white], up and [down], public money, [private] profit, leaps and [bounds]). It is weak or silent when the conjuncts are concrete nouns (salt and pepper, cat and dog) and when no coordinator precedes the word.

name: u22
explanation: Fires right after a verb meaning death, loss, destruction or going away (died, killed, lost, sank, escaped, passes away, disappear, depart, sent off), peaking on the next function word or particle (for, to, with, in, and, at, away, behind). It stays moderately active through the rest of that clause. The same structure after a neutral verb of arrival, finding, living or hiring stays near zero, and the verb token itself is usually weaker than the word after it.

name: u23
explanation: Dense, weakly selective unit whose clearest reliable trigger is the completeness adverb ' fully' placed after an auxiliary, copula or negation and before a participle/adjective ('have not been fully characterized', 'is not fully', 'are fully'), reaching ~0.5-0.9 of max; in long expository (scientific-abstract) context it also fires on a purpose-infinitive ' to' that follows a verb plus adverb ('have been used here to investigate', 'used widely to'). Most other tokens sit at a 0.0-0.5 background, so predict 'active' only for these slots and inactive for the same sentence with ' fully' replaced by another word or with the adverb/infinitive removed.

name: u24
explanation: Fires on a scope-setting function word that opens a phrase whose head is still to come: mainly quantifiers and negative or free-choice determiners ('any', 'no', 'nothing', 'whatever', 'only', 'most common', 'few', 'some'), and the do-support auxiliary ('did', 'does') after a relative 'who'. It is strongest for 'any' or 'nothing' right after a verb or preposition that sets up a request or offer ('Thanks for any', 'notified of any', 'ask for any', 'wanted nothing'). Plain articles ('the', 'a'), possessives, the following head noun and ordinary content words stay near zero.

name: u25
explanation: Lookahead unit that fires on the token right before a strongly expected preposition ' on'. It fires on words whose usual continuation is ' on', such as 'depending/depends', 'based', 'rely', 'impact/effect', 'closing in', 'and so', 'click', or a noun in an 'effect of X ... [noun] on Y' frame. It peaks on that word itself, and the following ' on' and words that do not predict ' on' ('according', 'trust', 'walking in', 'and then') stay near zero. Because it can only see earlier text, the activation is the same whether or not ' on' actually follows.

name: u26
explanation: Layer-0 unigram (token-identity) detector: it fires on the current token itself when that token is one of a semantically unrelated set of whole-word tokens, mainly ' dividends', ' gear', ' whispering', ' murderers', ' Richard', ' us', ' levels', ' know', ' false', ' center', ' employees', ' comforting', ' Association', ' house', and 'the' with no leading space (as in '\theta' or 'state-of-the-art'). Close synonyms or swaps ('profits', 'wheel', 'talking', 'killers', 'Robert', 'them', 'care') stay near the background level, and neither meaning nor the next token matters. The firing is strongest (about 0.5-1.0 of max) when the trigger comes 20 or more tokens into ordinary prose, and weaker (about 0.1-0.4) in very short texts.

name: u27
explanation: Absolute-position detector largely independent of token content: it is silent on tokens at positions below about 100 and between about 300 and 590, and fires on any token at absolute positions about 110-290 (peak near 160-210) and again at about 600-880 (peak near 720-780); content only scales the amplitude (varied/structured text such as code indentation or repeated 'Category:' lines fires harder than a run of 'the'). A text is predicted active if and only if it contains tokens in one of those position bands.

name: u28
explanation: Fires on an opening parenthesis '(' written directly against the preceding word or identifier with no space (function/method calls like print( or url(, math notation f(x), and plural markers like sheet(s)), and much more strongly the deeper the token is into a long document; a spaced ' (' or a '[' in the same place stays weak. It also has a diffuse, weaker (about 0.3-0.6 of max) background response on ordinary prose and code tokens late in long contexts, which the paren peak sits above.

name: u29
explanation: Mostly a positional unit: it fires on whatever word or word-piece sits at certain absolute token positions in the 128-token context (0-indexed), strongest at position 125, then 61-62, 86, 112, 74 and 47. Elsewhere it stays below about 0.3 of max. How high a hot position goes depends on the token there: ordinary words and word-pieces reach 0.4-1.0 of max, while punctuation and some tokens (e.g. ' sat', ' what') stay near 0. Shifting the text by one token moves the peak onto a different token, and short texts (under about 47 tokens) stay weak.

name: u30
explanation: Token-level detector with two related jobs, both strongest in programming/Q&A text: (1) the stem of a negative n't contraction (' don', ' didn', ' wouldn', ' haven'; weak on ' won', ' can'), firing on the stem and not on the uncontracted ' do'/' did'/' would'; (2) names from the Microsoft/.NET/SQL software stack (' Windows', ' Visual', ' SQL', 'Data' in System.Data, 'Connection', 'equ' of .equals), much weaker on the same words in lowercase everyday senses (' windows', ' data'). Smaller peaks on ' character' (especially 'characterised'), ' Community' and existential ' there'; ordinary content words, function words and other proper names stay near zero.

name: u31
explanation: A position-and-opening dial rather than a token detector: it is broadly active (about 0.4-0.9 of max) over roughly the first 20-30 tokens of a text, and it fades to near zero after about 40 tokens of fluent prose. Its level depends on how the text opens: it is highest when the text starts mid-stream or with an unusual opener (a rare word fragment such as 'Udzungwa', a lowercase 'the', 'Q:', a code line or a heading without an article), and it is low (under 0.35) when the text opens as a normal sentence with a capitalised 'The', 'Hello' or 'and'.

name: u32
explanation: A dense, low-selectivity context neuron (no sharp token set): it runs at a moderate level throughout source code, markup and structured data (Java/PHP/C++ declarations, JSON, CSS, wiki category lists) and is weak in plain narrative English prose (mostly below 0.2 of max). Within code it peaks on mid-statement keywords and identifiers such as ' static' after an access modifier, type names in generics, '();' and closing quote-bracket tokens, and its level builds with how much code-like context came before rather than with the peak token alone.

name: u33
explanation: A context-length-gated lexical neuron: it is nearly silent in the first few dozen tokens of a document (below ~0.2 of max). After roughly 100 or more tokens of context it fires on a small set of words, strongest on clause-final ' sometimes' ('it can be just perfect sometimes.'), capital ' U' that starts an abbreviation after 'the'/'after' (U.S., U.N., UUO), and ' whom', ' themselves', ' surprising', ' better' ending a phrase; near-synonyms such as ' usually', ' always', ' today', ' EU' or ' American' stay at the background level.

name: u34
explanation: Positional neuron: fires on almost any token whose absolute position in the context is roughly 110-250 (strongest about 140-215), with a weaker repeat band around positions 610-810, and is near zero elsewhere regardless of content (punctuation like '.' dips slightly within the band). It also has a small bump at positions 2-7 that is strongest on hyphens and hyphen-joined fragments (e.g. 'blood-', 'x-y-'); in the scan's windows the top examples are simply tokens late enough to reach the band's rising edge.

name: u35
explanation: Fires on the key slot word of a stock phrase in informational, commercial or reporting prose, where the slot holds a credential or quality adjective (best, expert, professional, master), an exact statistic numeral after a count, duration or survey verb ("is 90 days", "makes 55", "surveyed 1,500", "more than 20"), or the first-person pronoun in an epistemic hedge ("to the best of my", "as far as I"). It is weak for the same words in plain narrative ("the best singer", "bought 90 apples", "saw 3 dogs") and for vague quantifiers or ordinary adjectives in the same slot (many, several, same, new, tallest).

name: u36
explanation: A diffuse, weakly selective dial in GPT-2 L3. Its most reliable trigger is the preposition ' through', which reaches about 0.4-0.8 of max in short text and is highest in 'went/walked/passed through'. It also fires on travel nouns such as ' trip' and ' journey' after a determiner, and on ' Facebook' after 'on'/'a' in longer contexts. Synonyms in the same slot ('by', 'to', 'over', 'under', 'across', ' party', 'Twitter') give at most about 0.25. Many other content tokens and word pieces show a low background of 0.1-0.4, so text without these triggers is predicted to stay under about 0.3 of max.

name: u37
explanation: A dense, context-level register dial rather than a token detector: it is moderately active (about 0.3-1.0 of max) on most tokens in non-narrative web text such as code identifiers, citation markers, filmography or category lists, foreign-language titles, math drills and informal forum comments, with peaks on mid-list punctuation (`,` `)` `?`), sub-word pieces of identifiers (`Get`, `Site`, `v`) and clause-starting pronouns. It stays near zero in fluent, predictable narrative prose, especially on function words like ' the', ' a', ' was', and a story-like opening ('Once upon a time ...') suppresses it even on later code, citations or foreign titles.

name: u38
explanation: A dense, weakly selective neuron (background 0.1-0.5 of max on many prose tokens, rising slowly with context length) whose peaks fall on words that place an event ahead of the narrated time: desire or volition verbs ('wanted' before 'to'), the future auxiliary 'will' after a subject, and 'soon'. The noun 'youth' (in 'as a youth') is a second strong trigger. Near-synonyms without that prospective sense ('refused', 'planned', 'hoped', 'can', 'may', 'today', 'again', 'man') fire much less.

name: u39
explanation: A diffuse, context-gated neuron. It fires most reliably on a mid-word fragment that follows an accented or broken-up sub-word, most strongly 'mer' in Portuguese/Spanish 'números' (' n'+'ú'+'mer'; about 0.8 of max after 'Os', 0.3-0.5 in English frames). Elsewhere it gives scattered weak-to-moderate activity (0.1-0.5) across texts with fragmented tokenization, such as URLs, markup lines ('html', '======' under a link), Iberian-language prose and dense technical prose. Plain, short, cleanly tokenized English sentences and whole-word English equivalents ('numbers', 'number') stay near zero.
